conventions.statement: When n = 0, the index type Fin 0 is empty and the resulting Coxeter matrix is vacuously valid with no entries.
conventions.note: Junk-value: the empty matrix is a degenerate but well-typed Coxeter matrix.

conventions.statement: When n = 1, there is only one node and no off-diagonal entries; the Coxeter matrix is the 1×1 matrix [1] encoding the trivial Coxeter group.
conventions.note: Degenerate case with no edges in the diagram.

conventions.statement: When n = 2, the two nodes are simultaneously adjacent and the last pair, so the unique off-diagonal entry is 4, giving the dihedral group of order 8.
conventions.note: The weight-4 condition subsumes the weight-3 adjacency condition at n = 2.

conventions.statement: By convention the weight-4 (Bₙ-type) edge is always placed at the high-index end of the chain, between the nodes labelled n−1 and n−2, following the standard Bourbaki ordering.
conventions.note: This determines which end of the diagram is the 'B-end'.
